setup: Anchor the band at elbow height
Stand side-on, band in the far hand
Elbow bent to 90°, tucked at your side
A rolled towel under the arm helps
execution: Rotate your forearm out away from you
Keep the elbow pinned to your side
faults: Don't let the elbow drift away
Don't twist your body to help

notes: Use a light band. This is a small, controlled movement; go only as far as you can without the elbow leaving your side.
Check the band and anchor for wear before use, and anchor it to something that won't move.
Band tension isn't logged as a weight. Note the band colour if you want to track it.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain in the shoulder that builds during the set
Numbness or tingling in the arm

regressions.name: Lighter band
regressions.reason: Less tension while you learn to keep the elbow still.

progressions.name: Heavier band
progressions.reason: More tension once the full range is smooth.

progressions.name: 90/90 band external rotation
progressions.reason: Same rotation with the upper arm raised to shoulder height.

substitutions.name: Cable external rotation
substitutions.reason: Same movement on a stack, easier to load in small steps.

substitutions.name: Side-lying dumbbell external rotation
substitutions.reason: Lying on your side with a light dumbbell; no anchor needed.

substitutions.name: Face pull
substitutions.reason: Upper-back and rear-shoulder pull that ends with the hands rotating back.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Front view at chest height so the forearm swinging outward and the elbow staying at the side are clear. Band anchor drawn at the figure's side at elbow height.

keyPositions.label: Start
keyPositions.describe: Standing side-on to the anchor, working elbow bent to 90° and tucked at the side, forearm across the stomach holding the band.

keyPositions.label: End
keyPositions.describe: Forearm rotated outward, pointing forward-and-out, elbow still at the side and bent to 90°. Shoulder down.

ikHints: Elbow fixed against the side of the body
Band line runs from the anchor to the hand
emphasise: Elbow stays pinned to the side
doNotShow: Elbow drifting away from the body

uncertain.note: The main muscles are the rotator cuff (infraspinatus, teres minor). The vocabulary has no 'rotator_cuff' word (research Q1), so the nearest word, 'rear_delts', is used. This overstates the rear-delt role; the research file flags exactly this problem.
Mapped to 'horizontal_pull' (rear-shoulder work, like Face pull); the vocabulary has no rotation or prehab pattern.
'bodyweight' (no load recorded) is the usual convention for bands; band tension is never invented as kg (rule 6).
Approximate drawing targets. Negative shoulderExternalRotation means the forearm starts rotated in across the body.
